questions.stem: A student heats 10 g of calcium carbonate and collects the products. The solid residue weighs 5.6 g. What mass of carbon dioxide gas was released?
questions.explanation: By conservation of mass, the total mass of products equals the total mass of reactants. Mass of CO₂ = mass of reactant - mass of solid product = 10 g - 5.6 g = 4.4 g. No atoms are created or destroyed in a chemical reaction, so the 'missing' mass is accounted for by the gas that escaped.

questions.stem: When magnesium burns in air, the mass of the product (magnesium oxide) is greater than the mass of the original magnesium. Does this violate conservation of mass?

options.text: Yes, mass has been created during the reaction
No, the extra mass comes from the oxygen in the air combining with the magnesium
Yes, the burning process creates new atoms
No, the magnesium expanded during heating

questions.explanation: Conservation of mass is not violated. The magnesium reacts with oxygen from the air: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. The mass of MgO is greater than the mass of Mg alone because oxygen atoms from the air have combined with the magnesium. If you measured the total mass of Mg + O₂ before and MgO after, they would be equal.

questions.stem: What does the law of conservation of mass state?

options.text: Mass increases during exothermic reactions and decreases during endothermic reactions
Mass is always lost as heat energy during reactions
No atoms are created or destroyed in a chemical reaction, so the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products
The mass of products is always greater than the mass of reactants

questions.explanation: The law of conservation of mass states that in a chemical reaction, no atoms are created or destroyed. All atoms present in the reactants must be present in the products. This means the total mass of all reactants always equals the total mass of all products. Any apparent change in mass is due to gases entering or leaving the system.

questions.stem: A reaction between hydrochloric acid and sodium carbonate is carried out in an open beaker. The mass of the beaker and contents decreases during the reaction. What is the best explanation?

options.text: Some of the acid evaporated
The reaction produces carbon dioxide gas which escapes from the open beaker
Mass is destroyed during the reaction
The products are lighter than the reactants

questions.explanation: The reaction produces CO₂ gas: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. The carbon dioxide gas escapes from the open beaker into the atmosphere, causing an apparent decrease in mass. If the reaction were carried out in a sealed container, the total mass would remain constant. Mass is never destroyed in a chemical reaction.

questions.stem: Iron reacts with copper sulfate solution: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu. If 5.6 g of iron reacts with 16 g of copper sulfate, what is the total mass of the products?
questions.explanation: By conservation of mass, the total mass of products = total mass of reactants = 5.6 g + 16 g = 21.6 g. In this reaction, no gas is produced and all products remain in the solution or as a solid, so the mass is straightforward to account for. The 21.6 g is split between FeSO₄ in solution and solid Cu deposited.
